**Triage: lands on the seven converged rule-array `filter` doors in `packages/spec`; `domain:spec`; `priority:p2`; class (c).**

The seven `filter` doors converged on `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)` (the objectui#6206 family). On **the record form an author used to write**, they now refuse with a **bare `invalid_type`** — and **this package's own guidance convention is applied at none of them**. Measured on `origin/main` `501959b72`.

⇒ p2, and the reason is the transition: these doors *changed* what they accept, so the population hitting the refusal is exactly the authors who wrote the previously-legal form. ⭐ That is precisely when a refusal must name the new spelling — and instead it says the least useful thing zod can say.

⇒ Apply the package's existing guidance convention at all seven. ⛔ Do not invent a new message shape; the convention exists and using it is the point.

⚠️ **Downstream context, ⛔ not a fold:** objectui#8945 covers the same convergence from the consumer side (that repo's *"three shapes legitimately reach a renderer"* note is now half true). ⇒ same upstream event, two repos, two surfaces. Fix the messages here; ⛔ do not reach into objectui.

⚠️ Sibling family here, ⛔ not folded: objectstack#17299 (prescriptions buried in `invalid_union` sub-errors). Different mechanism, same user-visible outcome — an author who cannot see the guidance. ⭐ If one convention covers both, say so in the PR and the two can serialise.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

Clause-②: no — the change is to what a **refusal says**, not to what the doors accept. No key is added to any published payload, no accept set moves in either direction, and the seven doors keep refusing exactly the shapes they refuse today. ⚠️ If the round's measurement disagrees, **this seat** re-declares here — ⛔ the dev does not.

## Scope, from triage's own words

> Apply the package's existing guidance convention at all seven. ⛔ Do not invent a new message shape; the convention exists and using it is the point.

⭐ The card has already done the hardest part and the round inherits it rather than redoing it: the prescription is **not** missing — all seven `.describe()` strings already carry it, and the three `SemanticMigration` entries carry the full conversion table. **The gap is the runtime refusal, not the documentation**, because nothing bridges `.describe()` into a zod issue and this package has no global error map (`setErrorMap` / `z.config` → 0 under `packages/spec/src`, with `strictObject()`'s own `error` callback as the lit control that proves the probe reaches).

⚠️ The card also corrected itself before filing — a first draft claimed the prescription "ships only in the migration ledger", which is false. ⇒ ⛔ do not re-derive that claim from the draft; the corrected reading is the one in the body.

The three precedents the card names (`shared/expression.zod.ts`, `ui/view.zod.ts`, `shared/strict-object.ts`) are the convention. ⭐ The card says the third is the closest model and says why: **guidance derived from the schema rather than transcribed beside it, so it cannot drift.** That reasoning is binding on the shape of the fix — ⛔ a hand-copied sentence at seven sites is exactly what it argues against.

## File face declared

The seven declaring symbols' files — `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` (`ElementDataSourceSchema.filter`) and `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` (the six `ComponentPropsMap` doors) — plus pins and a changeset. ⛔ Declared NOT touched: the three migration entries, the `.describe()` strings (they already carry the prescription), and ⛔ **the objectui repo** — triage is explicit that objectui#8945 is the same upstream event from the consumer side and ⛔ not a fold.

⚠️ **Live overlap, declared**: PR #17835 (card #16929) is open on `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` and is **parked** — its card went to the decision box at 10:10Z over a release-shaping question, so it may sit for a while. ⇒ this round ⛔ does not wait on it; it merges `origin/main` before opening its PR, and whoever lands second resolves. ⛔ Do not edit #17835's hunks.

**Batch independence at 2026-09-12T10:24Z** — the other round in flight is #17594 (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, the generated registry region, an ADR-0087 disposition). Disjoint from this face. ⛔ Not folded.

## Closed out by CONTENT on `origin/main` `2d34f320d1` (2026-09-12T13:06Z), ⛔ not by the merge event

|:--|--:|

| a fabricated token across `ui/` | **0** (dark control) |

Both new files present as tracked blobs (`git ls-tree`, ⛔ not a content grep for a filename). ⭐ And the message was **read**, not counted — `filter-rule-array.ts:160-168` genuinely names the array form, the AND semantics of multiple record keys, and that legacy operator shorthands are normalized on parse:

> `` `filter` on ${surface} takes the ViewFilterRule ARRAY form … Write one rule per record key — they AND — … Legacy operator shorthands (`eq`, `gt`, `notIn`, …) are accepted and normalized on parse. ``

### The landing carried one disposition worth keeping on the record

Pre-check ② was **exit 4** with **seven** T1 widening tells. ⛔ The declaration was not flipped. I read the diff at all seven doors myself: each is `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)` → `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, { error: … })`, with the key name, its optionality and **the element schema byte-identical**. An `error` param chooses the message on a **refusal**; there is no input it causes to be accepted. The round measured the same from the other end — `json-schema/` and the authorable-surface artifacts byte-identical after two full builds.

The C5 row is **report-only by its own words**, and my landing checklist had been treating it as a blocker — which parked three PRs today. Corrected discipline, recorded on the PR: **the row stands until a direct reading of the thing it claims overturns it, per PR.** The instrument defect and its two siblings are filed as **#17848**.

### What this round did that is worth carrying forward

⭐ **Its ablation had two legs that differ by exactly one case** — unwiring the seven doors reds 12 pins; neutralising the helper reds the same 12 **plus the helper's own unit pin**. Two legs that red identically would not have distinguished the wiring from the helper.

⭐ **And one leg did not happen and was reported as such**: a quoting error wrote nothing, the on-disk marker count came back 0, and the guard **refused the run rather than reporting a green ablation over an unmutated tree**. That is the vacuous pass caught by its own control.

Seven doors got **seven separate before/after readings** against the built artifact — ⛔ not one generalised — each with door-shaped negative controls proving the ordinary messages are untouched.
